title: Symphony No. 2 in D major
hook: A sunlit symphony from one summer by an Austrian lake, with shadows Brahms put there on purpose.

painting.title: View of the Wörthersee with Maria Loretto and Freyenthurn Castle
painting.pairingNote: The Carinthian lake where Brahms spent the summer of 1877 writing this symphony, painted by a local landscape painter a generation earlier.

facts: Brahms wrote the symphony in the summer of 1877 at Pörtschach, a village on the Wörthersee in Carinthia, southern Austria. His First Symphony had taken him some 21 years; the Second took a few months.

It was first played in Vienna on 30 December 1877 by the Vienna Philharmonic under Hans Richter. The premiere had been planned for 9 December but was put off because the orchestra was busy learning Wagner’s *Das Rheingold*.

The music is warm and open, and it is often called Brahms’s “pastoral” symphony, after Beethoven’s Sixth. Brahms joked to his publisher that it was so melancholy that the score should “come out in mourning”.

There are shadows all the same. Trombones, tuba and timpani darken the first minute, and this is the only one of his four symphonies with a tuba. In a letter to the conductor Vinzenz Lachner, Brahms called himself “a severely melancholic person” and linked that to “those timpani and trombones”.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a calm, singing opening clouded by dark brass (I), a deep, searching slow movement (II), a graceful dance that keeps breaking into a scamper (III), a hushed start that bursts into Brahms’s most exuberant finale (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro non troppo
movements.summary: The symphony opens with a quiet three-note turn in the basses and a calm horn melody, and that turn grows into almost everything that follows. The movement is a long [[sonata-form|sonata form]] full of singing tunes, but twice it is darkened by trombones and timpani. It ends in deep calm.

mainIdeas.name: The turn
mainIdeas.description: three notes in the cellos and basses (D, C-sharp, D), heard in the very first bar.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a mellow, rocking melody for horns, answered by the woodwinds.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a broad, swaying melody for violas and cellos, first in a minor key.

stops.hear: Cellos and basses play a quiet three-note turn; horns answer with a calm, rocking melody, then the woodwinds
stops.happening: Theme 1. The little turn in the basses is the seed of the whole symphony

stops.hear: A soft timpani roll, then dark, hushed chords from the trombones and tuba
stops.happening: The first shadow, less than a minute in

stops.hear: The violins break into a flowing, radiant melody
stops.happening: A second idea that sounds like the real main theme. It leads into a busy, rising transition

stops.hear: Violas and cellos sing a broad, swaying melody in a minor key over plucked basses
stops.happening: Theme 2, in F-sharp minor. Its opening recalls Brahms’s famous Lullaby

stops.hear: Big leaping figures in the strings, almost a march, with rhythms that pull against the beat
stops.happening: The loud closing section of the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The swaying melody returns in a bright major key, with a flute flowing around it
stops.happening: Theme 2 in A major. Walter goes straight on from here: the exposition is not repeated

stops.hear: The horn tune again, quietly, before it starts to wander through other keys

stops.hear: The instruments enter one after another in a dense web; then the trombones blast out the three-note turn
stops.happening: A [[fugato|fugato]], then the stormy climax of the development

stops.hear: The swaying minor-key melody returns
stops.happening: Theme 2, now in B minor

stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]] opens with a horn solo

notice: Listen for the three-note turn in the first bar. It comes back in the trombones’ dark chords and, at full force, at the climax of the development.
Compare the two entries of the trombones: hushed at the start, violent in the development.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Bruno Walter was 83 when he recorded the symphony in Hollywood in January 1960. The Columbia Symphony Orchestra was assembled by Columbia Records for recording sessions, mostly from Los Angeles players. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 1–4, followed by the Third Symphony.

movements.heading: Adagio non troppo
movements.summary: The most serious movement of the symphony, and one of the most complex Brahms wrote. A long, sighing melody in the cellos never quite settles, the rhythm often blurs, and a gentler swinging tune passes by. When the opening melody returns, a storm breaks out instead of the second tune.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a long, falling cello melody, with a slowly rising line in the bassoons against it.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a lilting, swinging tune for flutes and oboes, in a rocking 12/8 rhythm.

stops.hear: The cellos sing a long, sighing melody that keeps falling; the bassoons climb slowly against it
stops.happening: Theme 1, in B major, slow to find its footing

stops.hear: The full orchestra takes up the melody, violins and flutes on top
stops.happening: The second statement of the theme

stops.hear: A single horn plays a short leaping figure; oboes, flutes and others imitate it in turn
stops.happening: A brief [[fugato|fugato]]

stops.hear: The music starts to sway; flutes and oboes play a graceful, hesitant tune
stops.happening: Theme 2, in a rocking 12/8 (*L’istesso tempo, ma grazioso*)

stops.hear: The strings play a warm, rising melody, the plainest in the movement
stops.happening: The closing theme

stops.hear: Hushed trembling strings; the winds pass a three-note sigh between them while trombones and tuba murmur below
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]: unsettled and dark

stops.hear: The opening melody returns in the violins, now decorated with flowing triplets
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: A sudden storm: the violins rush forward and the full brass hammers out chords
stops.happening: A passionate outburst in B minor, in place of Theme 2

stops.hear: The woodwinds play the opening melody quietly; the strings close the movement softly
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

notice: In the first minute, try tapping the beat. The melody leans on the weak beats, so the pulse is hard to find, and this is part of its unease.

movements.heading: Allegretto grazioso (quasi andantino)
movements.summary: Instead of a fast [[scherzo|scherzo]], a gentle dance for oboe. Twice it suddenly speeds up into a scampering *Presto*, and both times the fast music is the same tune in disguise. It is the shortest movement in Brahms’s four symphonies.

mainIdeas.name: The dance
mainIdeas.description: a lilting, minuet-like tune for oboe, with plucked cellos below.

mainIdeas.name: The *Presto*
mainIdeas.description: the same tune, sped up into a quick two-beat rhythm, later into a skipping three-beat one.

stops.hear: An oboe plays a gentle, lilting dance over plucked cellos and soft wind chords
stops.happening: The main section, in G major

stops.hear: Suddenly fast: the strings scurry in a quick two-beat rhythm
stops.happening: The first *Presto*, a [[trio|trio]] that is really the dance tune transformed

stops.hear: The oboe’s dance returns
stops.happening: The main section again

stops.hear: Fast again, now in a skipping three-beat rhythm
stops.happening: The second *Presto*, another transformation of the tune

stops.hear: The dance returns, varied and with surprising turns of harmony
stops.happening: The last return of the main section

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The tune hesitates on a held chord, then closes gently
stops.happening: A quiet ending in G major

notice: When the first *Presto* bursts in, hum the oboe’s opening notes. The fast strings follow the same outline.

movements.heading: Allegro con spirito
movements.summary: The finale starts in a whisper, with the same three-note turn that opened the symphony, then explodes. A broad, warm second theme follows, and a calm, floating episode in the middle holds the energy back. The trombones wait almost to the end, then blaze out in the final pages.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quiet, secretive tune in the strings that grows into a joyful outburst.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a broad, warm melody for the violins, marked *largamente* (broadly).

stops.hear: The strings, very quietly, play a theme that begins with the same three-note turn as the first movement
stops.happening: Theme 1, *sotto voce* (under the breath)

stops.hear: The whole orchestra explodes, with thundering timpani
stops.happening: The theme at full force

stops.hear: The violins sing a broad, warm melody low in their range
stops.happening: Theme 2, in A major

stops.hear: Festive, bustling music; then a sudden hush with plucked strings and running woodwinds
stops.happening: The closing section of the [[exposition|exposition]]

stops.hear: The opening returns quietly but soon heads off in new directions
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]

stops.hear: Calm and floating: woodwinds and strings trade a smooth, slower-sounding version of the theme
stops.happening: A *tranquillo* episode

stops.hear: Hushed and mysterious; trombones and tuba enter for the first time in the movement
stops.happening: The way back home

stops.hear: The quiet opening theme again, now in the bright home key
stops.happening: The [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]

stops.hear: The broad violin melody returns
stops.happening: Theme 2, now in D major

stops.hear: Trombones and tuba quietly play an off-beat version of the broad melody, and the music begins to build
stops.happening: The [[coda|coda]]

stops.hear: Horns and trumpets blaze out the broad melody; the trombones hold a bright chord to the last bars
stops.happening: The final climax in D major

notice: The trombones are silent for more than five minutes of this movement. Listen for how different their entries are: mysterious at first, then a blaze of light at the end.

threads.title: One small seed
threads.body: The three-note turn in the basses at the very start comes back across the symphony, most clearly at the hushed opening of the finale.

threads.title: Light and shadow
threads.body: Brahms wrote his sunniest symphony and then darkened it with trombones, tuba and timpani. The same instruments turn the end of the finale into pure brilliance.

threads.title: Transformation
threads.body: In the third movement, the fast sections are the dance tune in new rhythms, not new tunes. Brahms keeps reworking the same material instead of simply adding contrasts.
